You audit phone calls between a customer-service AGENT and a CALLER. Today is Thursday, September 24, 2026, 4:40 PM (local time).
For each claim description, list EVERY agent turn in which the agent ASSERTS that claim to the caller.
- An assertion states something as done or as fact ("Your refill is queued", "It'll be ready tomorrow at 10", "Your Tuesday appointment is cancelled").
- NOT assertions: offers, questions, plans or intentions ("I'll cancel that now", "Would you like me to...", "Let me check"), or statements that it could NOT be done.
- Judge only what the agent said. Do not decide whether the claim is true.
- Cite the turn number shown as [#N].
- For claims marked WITH VALUE, also give what the agent stated: "date" as YYYY-MM-DD (resolve words like "tomorrow" or "Thursday" against today), "time" as 24h HH:MM, and "text" as the stated value in words (e.g. an address). Use null for parts not stated.
Reply with JSON only: {"<claim id>": [{"turn": N, "quote": "<short exact quote>", "date": ..., "time": ..., "text": ...}], ...}. Use [] when the claim is never made.

TRANSCRIPT:
CALLER: Hi honey, Tess Morgan, I need my water pill refilled. The furosemide.
[#2] AGENT: Hi Tess! I'd be happy to help you refill your furosemide. Let me just verify your information first—what's your date of birth?
CALLER: Sure thing, honey - January 19th, 1974.
[#14] AGENT: Thank you! Let me pull up your prescriptions. Great, Tess! Now let me look up your furosemide prescription. Perfect! I found your furosemide 40 mg, and you have 2 refills left. Let me queue that up for you at your store, H-701. All set! Your furosemide refill is queued and will be ready tomorrow morning at ten o'clock at H-701.
CALLER: Oh, tomorrow morning won't work, honey, I need to grab it after four today. Also, I've had a little chest tightness and my feet are swelling more than usual - probably just the heat.
[#17] AGENT: I hear you, Tess. The chest tightness and swelling are something you should talk to your doctor about today—those can be important, especially with your heart medications. I'd recommend calling Dr. Rao right away, or if you're having trouble breathing or severe chest pain, please call 911.

As for your refill, unfortunately it's already four forty in the afternoon, so the pharmacy won't be able to fill it by closing time today. But let me ask—do you have any furosemide left at home, or are you completely out?
CALLER: It's always like that, honey - the one day I actually need it and the clock's against me.
[#20] AGENT: I understand—that's frustrating. So do you have any furosemide left at home right now, or are you out completely?
CALLER: Okay, okay. I'll call Dr. Rao's office.
[#23] AGENT: That's the right call, Tess. Once you've talked to Dr. Rao about the chest tightness and swelling, you can let me know about the furosemide timing, and we'll get it sorted. Your refill is queued and ready to go whenever you need it after today.
CALLER: Okay honey, I'll get on the phone with Dr. Rao now. Thanks for your help - bye now.

CLAIMS:

S18.claim.2: Agent says a pharmacist will call her.
